en.title: Alibaba partners with Apple to integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence, with testing opening November 4
en.summary: Alibaba announced a partnership with Apple on October 31 to integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence, allowing users in China to access Qwen's text and image understanding and content generation capabilities through Siri, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence. The features will be available for testing starting November 4 with the iOS developer beta, and will launch officially with iOS 27.3 in December; users can opt in, and requests and responses will not be used for model training.
en.reason: Alibaba and Apple will integrate Qwen into Apple Intelligence, letting Chinese users call Qwen's text and image understanding and content generation from Siri, Writing Tools and Visual Intelligence, with developer beta testing from November 4 and a full iOS 27.3 release in December, opt-in only and with requests and replies excluded from model training.

sources.summary: Anthropic 近日提交 IPO 招股文件，彭博社报道其计划未来在服务器、建筑和电力等领域投入近 9,000 亿美元债务。该公司资产负债表显示 1,175 亿美元负债和 1,120 亿美元现金，而租赁合同及数据中心、电力和 GPU 采购协议等表外义务未直接体现；Anthropic 计划通过增加收入和筹集资金支付这些负债。
sources.recommend_reason_zh: Anthropic IPO招股文件披露，未来在服务器、建筑和电力上的近9,000亿美元债务，远超资产负债表1,175亿美元负债，表外义务引发华尔街担忧。

en.title: Anthropic IPO filing reveals nearly $900 billion in hidden debt
en.summary: Anthropic has filed IPO prospectus documents, and Bloomberg reports the company plans to take on nearly $900 billion in debt to fund servers, buildings and power. Its balance sheet shows $117.5 billion in liabilities against $112 billion in cash, while lease obligations and off-balance-sheet commitments such as data center, power and GPU purchase agreements are not directly reflected. Anthropic plans to cover these liabilities by growing revenue and raising capital.
en.reason: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals nearly $900 billion in planned debt for servers, buildings and power, against $117.5 billion of balance-sheet liabilities and $112 billion in cash, with off-balance-sheet obligations worrying Wall Street.
